schema: app | feature | currentRoute | standardDestination | liquidDestination | keyboardRoute | dataStateOwner | automatedProof | visualProof | status
rule: A row closes on an observed side effect, never on a control's presence. `observed` carries the literal before/after measurement; a row with no `observed` is explicitly not proven.

statusVocabulary.standard-only: deliberately never going Liquid; reason required inline
statusVocabulary.both: verified in standard and Liquid, each by side effect
statusVocabulary.REGRESSION: reachable in one and not the other; blocks the wave

Detach `transcript` returned ok:true and /health gained window id 3 at 1050,390 460x820 — dead-centre of the 2560x1600 primary work area ((2560-460)/2=1050, (1600-820)/2=390) — rendering a real Transcript panel with honest empty states ("Waiting for the player…", "No subtitle track is loaded.") and no fabricated cues. Reattach: clicking the detached window's own `Return to the player` destroyed window 4 and the host received exactly 1 `studyblock:changed` broadcast carrying `[]`. TRAP: `studyBlockClose` resolves BEFORE the window's `closed` event, so a same-tick `studyBlockList()` still returned the entry and only settled to 0 on the next tick; the UI is unaffected because it listens to `studyblock:changed`, but a caller that closes-then-lists reads stale.

Move to the second display: ok:true, /health bounds 1050,390 460x820 -> 2730,20 460x560. x=2560+(800-460)/2=2730 is the requested centring; the 820 -> 560 height is the OS clamping to a 600-tall monitor, and `rememberBounds` persisted the ACTUAL 560, not the requested 820. Close/reopen: after close the window reopened as id 4 at 2730,20 460x560 — identical in all four numbers, still on the second monitor. Geometry file was ABSENT before the run and was deleted afterwards, restoring userData.
